question: Should OpenClaw adopt this cross-cutting localization runtime, readiness-gate model, and Gateway metadata contract as the direction for the five-PR foundation series?
rationale: The patch introduces a broad permanent architecture and compatibility surface rather than a narrowly established bug fix; the correct ownership boundaries, release claims, and adoption order require maintainer product judgment.

options.title: Sponsor a staged localization foundation
options.body: Confirm the RFC direction and require each dependent bundle to be independently rebased, scoped, compatibility-reviewed, and proven before merge.

options.title: Narrow to an existing surface
options.body: Retain only a specific approved localization repair, such as one Control UI or channel presentation gap, and defer the shared runtime and readiness architecture.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Leave the draft open but do not merge the cumulative architecture until maintainers choose a supported localization product boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged localization foundation
recommendation.body: Confirm the RFC direction and require each dependent bundle to be independently rebased, scoped, compatibility-reviewed, and proven before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The item already carries protected maintainer handling, but the supplied context does not establish a reliable individual current-main owner.
